# Proofload

> Load testing for the JVM, written in Kotlin. A scenario is an ordinary Kotlin
> value. Departures follow a schedule that responses cannot change, every step
> is timed on two clocks (service time, and response time = service time plus
> the user's departure lateness), and every run records whether the generator
> kept its schedule, so a slow generator can be told apart from a slow target.
> A load test is an ordinary JUnit 5, Kotest or zio-test test, or a plain `main`.

Facts worth having before anything else:

- Kotlin 2.4, JVM 21+, Apache 2.0. Virtual threads on the JDK's own HTTP client.
- `0.1.0-rc4` is the current release on Maven Central. Coordinates are
  `io.github.matthewjones372:proofload-core` and its siblings, such as
  `proofload-http`, `proofload-junit5` and `proofload-report-html`.
  `proofload-core` depends on the Kotlin standard library and nothing else;
  every client, test framework and report format is a separate module.
- A step is named once: `step("place order")` gives a `StepName`, and the same
  handle indexes the result, `result[placeOrder]`. Session values are typed the
  same way: `sessionKey<String>("orderId")`.
- Checks belong on the request (`expecting(201)`, `checking("has an id") { }`).
  A failed step is counted, not thrown, with its `Reason`, and ends that user's
  journey: `result[placeOrder].failed.count`, `failedWith(HttpStatus(503))`.
- Nothing fails a run for falling behind unless asked: declare `keptSchedule`
  as a goal, assert `result.metEveryGoal`, and check `result.lostGround()`.
  `metEveryGoal` is true for a run with no goals.
- A simulation is a value: `checkout.at(50.perSecond, over = 1.minutes)` has
  3,000 users before anything runs.

## The shape of a test

`@LoadTest` is `@Test` with a `Proofload` parameter, here against a JDK `HttpServer`.

```kotlin
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.at
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.engine.Proofload
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.fedBy
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.feed
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.http.http
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.junit5.LoadTest
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.perSecond
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.scenario
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.sessionKey
import io.github.matthewjones372.proofload.step
import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

private val orderId = sessionKey<String>("orderId")
private val customer = sessionKey<String>("customer")

private val browse = step("browse")
private val placeOrder = step("place order")

class CheckoutLoadTest {

    @LoadTest
    fun `checkout holds up at fifty a second`(proofload: Proofload) {
        val api = http.baseUrl("http://localhost:${server.address.port}")

        val checkout = scenario("checkout") {
            exec(browse, api.get("/products/{customer}"))
            exec(
                placeOrder,
                api.post("/orders")
                    .body("""{"cart":"1 anvil"}""")
                    .expecting(201)
                    .capture(orderId) { response -> response.header("location") },
            )
        }

        val result = proofload.run(
            checkout.at(50.perSecond, over = 1.seconds)
                .fedBy(feed(customer) { user -> "customer-$user" }),
        )

        result[browse].count shouldBe 50L
        result[placeOrder].failed.count shouldBe 0L
    }
}
```

## What it will not do

- No `Thread.sleep` pacing: departures are scheduled. Think time is
  `pause(200.milliseconds)` in the scenario.
- No interpolation: a percentile is the top of the bucket a sample landed in.
- No registry, nothing to run at startup, and no `main` of its own.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/README.md): the problem, the approach, an example.
- [Getting started](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md): a complete first test.
- [How Proofload measures](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/docs/measurement.md): the two clocks, the schedule checks, what a run does not establish.
- [Cookbook index](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/docs/cookbook.md): every recipe, by task.
- [For agents](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/docs/for-agents.md): every public signature, and the mistakes to avoid.
- [Modules](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/docs/modules.md): each module and its dependencies.
- [Invariants](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/docs/invariants.md): what a trustworthy result depends on, and what does not hold yet.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/matthewjones372/proofload/blob/main/AGENTS.md): for working on Proofload, not with it.
